questions.stem:
Keith records the amount of rainfall, in mm, at his school, each day for a week. The results are given below.

2.8   5.6   2.3   9.4   0.0   0.5   1.8

Jenny then records the amount of rainfall, $x$ mm, at the school each day for the following 21 days. The results for the 21 days are summarised below.

$\sum x = 84.6$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the mean amount of rainfall during the whole 28 days.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for a clear attempt to add the two sums. Accept a full expression or $2.8+5.6+…+84.6=x$ where $100<x<110$ i.e. seeing at least two correct terms of Keith's and the 84.6 with a slip.
A1: for awrt 3.8 (Condone 1 dp/2sf here since data is given to 1 dp or 2 sf). Accept $\frac{107}{28}$ or $3\frac{23}{28}$ or any exact equivalent.
Correct answer implies M1A1.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $2.8 + 5.6 + 2.3 + 9.4 + 0.5 + 1.8 + 84.6 = 107$ M1
- mean $= 107 / 28$ (= 3.821… ) (awrt 3.8) A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Keith realises that he has transposed two of his figures. The number 9.4 should have been 4.9 and the number 0.5 should have been 5.0. Keith corrects these figures.
(b) State, giving your reason, the effect this will have on the mean.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for clearly stating that it will have no effect. ("roughly the same" is B0)
dB1: for a supporting reason that mentions the fact that the increase and decrease are the same and gives some numerical value(s) to support this, e.g. sum of Keith's observations is still 22.4 (or mean is still 3.2) or sum is still 107 or $9.4-4.9=5-0.5$ (o.e.). This second B1 is dependent on their saying there is no effect so B0B1 is not possible.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- It will have no effect since B1 one is 4.5 under what it should be and the other is 4.5 above what it should be. dB1

questions.stem:
Over a long period of time a small company recorded the amount it received in sales per month. The results are summarised below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline & \text{Amount received in sales (£1000s)}\\ \hline \text{Two lowest values} & 3, 4\\ \hline \text{Lower quartile} & 7\\ \hline \text{Median} & 12\\ \hline \text{Upper quartile} & 14\\ \hline \text{Two highest values} & 20, 25\\ \hline\end{array}$

An outlier is an observation that falls
either $1.5 \times$ interquartile range above the upper quartile
or $1.5 \times$ interquartile range below the lower quartile.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) On the graph paper below, draw a box plot to represent these data, indicating clearly any outliers.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
A fully correct box-plot (either version) with no supporting work scores 5/5. Otherwise read on.
M1: for at least one correct calculation seen.
A1: for 24.5 and $-3.5$ (or just negative noted) seen. May be read off the graph. If both values are seen but no calculation is given then M1A1, one value M1A0.
M1: for a box with an upper and a lower whisker(s) with at least 2 correct values (condone no median marked).
A1ft: for 3,7,12,14 and 20 or 24.5 in appropriate places and readable off their scale. If both upper whiskers are seen A0. Apply ft for their whiskers being compatible with their outlier limits, e.g. if their lower limit is $+3.5$ then a lower whisker ending at 4 or 3.5 is OK.
B1: for only one outlier appropriately marked at 25.
Apply $\pm 0.5$ square accuracy for diagram.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Outliers $14 + 1.5\times(14-7) = 24.5$ M1
- $7 - 1.5\times(14-7) = -3.5$ A1
- Outlier 25 either upper limit acceptable on diagram

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) State the skewness of the distribution of the amount of sales received. Justify your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for $Q_3-Q_2 < Q_2-Q_1$ statement or an equivalent statement in words. Use of $Q_3-Q_2 < Q_2-Q_1$ does not require differences to be seen.
dB1: for "negative skew" dependent on suitable reason given above. "correlation" is B0. "positive skew" with a supporting argument based on whiskers can score B1B1, e.g. "right hand whisker is longer than LH one so positive skew". $Q_3-Q_2 < Q_2-Q_1$ followed by "positive skew" is B1B0.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) The company claims that for 75% of the months, the amount received per month is greater than £10 000. Comment on this claim, giving a reason for your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for rejecting the company's claim.
dB1: for an appropriate supporting reason (dependent on rejecting the company's claim), e.g. since the lower quartile is 7000 and therefore 75% above 7000 not 10000, or 10 is inside the box, or any other sensible comment.

questions.stem:
On a randomly chosen day, each of the 32 students in a class recorded the time, $t$ minutes, to the nearest minute, they spent on their homework. The data for the class is summarised in the following table.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Time, } t & \text{Number of students}\\ \hline 10-19 & 2\\ \hline 20-29 & 4\\ \hline 30-39 & 8\\ \hline 40-49 & 11\\ \hline 50-69 & 5\\ \hline 70-79 & 2\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use interpolation to estimate the value of the median.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for an attempt to use interpolation to find the median. Condone use of 39 or 40 for 39.5, e.g. allow $39+\frac{2}{11}\times 10$ (o.e.) or $40+\frac{2}{11}\times 10$ (o.e.) to score M1A0 but must have the 10.
A1: for awrt 41.3 (or awrt 41.8 if using $(n+1)$).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Median = 32/2 = 16th term (16.5) $\frac{x-39.5}{49.5-39.5}=\frac{16-14}{25-14}$ or $x=39.5+\left(\frac{2}{11}\times 10\right)$ M1
- Median = 41.3 ( use of $n + 1$ gives 41.8) (awrt 41.3) A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that

$\sum t = 1414$ and $\sum t^2 = 69378$

(b) find the mean and the standard deviation of the times spent by the students on their homework.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for awrt 44.2.
M1: for a correct expression including square root. (Allow ft of their mean).
A1: for awrt 14.7 (If using $s$ for awrt 14.9). You may see $\sum t = 1339 \to \bar{t}=41.8$ and $\sum t^2 = 62928 \to \sigma = 14.7$ or $s = 14.9$ this scores B0 for the mean but can score M1 for a correct st.dev expression and A1 for ans. Correct answer only in (a) and (b) can score full marks but check $(n+1)$ case in (a).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Mean$=\frac{1414}{32}=44.1875$ (awrt 44.2) B1
- Standard deviation $=\sqrt{\frac{69378}{32}-\left(\frac{1414}{32}\right)^2}$ M1 $= 14.7$ (or $s = 14.9$) A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Comment on the skewness of the distribution of the times spent by the students on their homework. Give a reason for your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1ft: for a correct comparison of their mean and their median (may be in a formula). Calculating median − mean as negative is OK for this B1 but must say +ve skew for 2nd B1. Only allow comparison to be $\approx 0$ if $|\text{mean}-\text{median}| \leqslant 0.5$.
B1ft: for a correct description of skewness based on their values of mean and median, ft their values for mean and median not their previous calculation/comparison. Must be compatible with their previous comparison (if they have one). "Positive skew" with no reason is B0B1 provided you can see their values that imply that. Description should be "positive" or "negative" or "no" skew or "symmetric". "Positive correlation" is B0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- mean > median therefore positive skew B1ft B1ft
- Quartiles 1st B1ft if $Q_1$ = awrt 32 and $Q_3$ = awrt 49 seen and a correct comparison made. ft $Q_2$ 2nd B1ft if $Q_1$ = awrt 32 or $Q_3$ = awrt 49 seen and a correct description based on their quartiles and their comparison is made. (Should get "negative skew")

questions.stem:
The bag $P$ contains 6 balls of which 3 are red and 3 are yellow.
The bag $Q$ contains 7 balls of which 4 are red and 3 are yellow.
A ball is drawn at random from bag $P$ and placed in bag $Q$. A second ball is drawn at random from bag $P$ and placed in bag $Q$.
A third ball is then drawn at random from the 9 balls in bag $Q$.

The event $A$ occurs when the 2 balls drawn from bag $P$ are of the same colour.
The event $B$ occurs when the ball drawn from bag $Q$ is red.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the tree diagram shown below.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for both $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{1}{3}$ shown correctly on the diagram.
B1: for $\frac{4}{9}$ shown correctly on the diagram.
B1: for both $\frac{3}{5}$, $\frac{2}{5}$ shown correctly on the diagram.
B1: for all three of $\frac{4}{9}$, $\frac{4}{9}$, $\frac{5}{9}$ shown correctly on the diagram.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: for $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}$ (oe) seen at least once.
M1: $\mathrm{P}(A) = \mathrm{P}(RR)+\mathrm{P}(YY) = \frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{2}\times\text{"}\frac{2}{5}\text{"} = \frac{2}{5}$.
A1: for $\frac{2}{5}$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for both cases, and +, attempted, ft their values from tree diagram. May be 4 cases of 3 balls.

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for at least 1 case of 3 balls identified (implied by 2nd M1).
M1: for all 4 correct expressions $\mathrm{P}(B)=\mathrm{P}(RRR)+\mathrm{P}(RYR)+\mathrm{P}(YRR)+\mathrm{P}(YYR)$, ft their values from tree diagram.
$\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\text{"}\frac{2}{3}\text{"}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{5}{9}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\text{"}\frac{3}{5}\text{"}\times\frac{5}{9}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\text{"}\frac{2}{5}\text{"}\times\text{"}\frac{4}{9}\text{"}\right)=\frac{5}{9}$ (*)
A1cso: correct answer only, must see evidence for M1.

parts.label: d
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for identifying both cases and + probs. $\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)=\mathrm{P}(RRR)+\mathrm{P}(YYR)$. May be implied by correct expressions $=\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{4}{9}\right)$
A1cso: $=\frac{2}{9}$ (*).

parts.label: e
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for use of $\mathrm{P}(A\cup B)=\mathrm{P}(A)+\mathrm{P}(B)-\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)$. Must have some attempt to use the formula.
$=\text{"}\frac{2}{5}\text{"}+\frac{5}{9}-\frac{2}{9}=\frac{11}{15}$
A1cao.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for clear attempt to use the correct formula, must have some correct substitution. ft their (b)

parts.label: f
parts.text:
(f) Given that all three balls drawn are the same colour, find the probability that they are all red.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for identifying the correct probabilities and forming appropriate fraction of probs.
$\frac{\mathrm{P}(RRR)}{\mathrm{P}(RRR)+\mathrm{P}(YYY)}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{2}{3}}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{9}\right)}$
A1ft: for a correct expression using probabilities from their tree, probabilities must come from the product of 3 probs. from their tree diagram.
A1cao: $=\frac{6}{11}$. Accept exact decimal equivalents. Correct answer only is full marks except in (c) and (d).

questions.stem:
The weight, $X$ grams, of soup put in a tin by machine $A$ is normally distributed with a mean of 160 g and a standard deviation of 5 g.
A tin is selected at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that this tin contains more than 168 g.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for an attempt to standardize 168 with 160 and 5 i.e. $\pm\left(\frac{168-160}{5}\right)$ or implied by 1.6.
A1: for $\mathrm{P}(Z>1.6)$ or $\mathrm{P}(Z<-1.6)$ i.e. $z=1.6$ and a correct inequality or 1.6 on a shaded diagram.
A1: awrt 0.0548. Correct answer to (a) implies all 3 marks.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{P}(X>168)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{168-160}{5}\right)$ M1 $=\mathrm{P}(Z>1.6)$ A1 $=0.0548$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The weight stated on the tin is $w$ grams.
(b) Find $w$ such that $\mathrm{P}(X<w)=0.01$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for attempting $\pm\left(\frac{w-160}{5}\right)=$ recognizable $z$ value ($|z|>1$).
B1: for $z=\pm 2.3263$ or better. Should be $z=…$ or implied so: $1-2.3263=\frac{w-160}{5}$ is M0B0.
A1: for awrt 148. This may be scored for other $z$ values so M1B0A1 is possible. For awrt 148 only with no working seen award M1B0A1.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{P}(X<w)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{w-160}{5}\right)$ $\frac{w-160}{5}=-2.3263$ M1 B1 $w=148.37$ awrt 148 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The weight, $Y$ grams, of soup put into a carton by machine $B$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ grams and standard deviation $\sigma$ grams.
(c) Given that $\mathrm{P}(Y<160)=0.99$ and $\mathrm{P}(Y>152)=0.90$ find the value of $\mu$ and the value of $\sigma$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for attempting to standardize 160 or 152 with $\mu$ and $\sigma$ (allow $\pm$) and equate to $z$ value ($|z|>1$).
B1: for awrt $\pm 2.33$ or $\pm 2.32$ seen.

questions.question_text:
The weight, $X$ grams, of soup put in a tin by machine $A$ is normally distributed with a mean of 160 g and a standard deviation of 5 g.
A tin is selected at random.
(a) Find the probability that this tin contains more than 168 g.
(3)
The weight stated on the tin is $w$ grams.
(b) Find $w$ such that $\mathrm{P}(X<w)=0.01$
(3)
The weight, $Y$ grams, of soup put into a carton by machine $B$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ grams and standard deviation $\sigma$ grams.
(c) Given that $\mathrm{P}(Y<160)=0.99$ and $\mathrm{P}(Y>152)=0.90$ find the value of $\mu$ and the value of $\sigma$.
(6)
